stories.title: Google ordered to open Android and Search to rivals in Europe
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The EU has mandated that Google must grant rivals greater access to core components of Android and Google Search.
This ruling is part of the EU's enforcement of digital antitrust regulations against Google.
The decision threatens to reduce Google's dominance over two of the industry's most critical platforms.

stories.title: OnePlus officially gives up on the US and Europe
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: OnePlus is officially exiting the US and European markets.
The brand will cease launching new products in these regions.
Existing customers will receive continued support and updates via Oppo's ColorOS.

stories.title: xAI sues a man for using Grok to generate CSAM ‘deepfakes’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: xAI is suing an individual for allegedly using its Grok AI chatbot to generate CSAM.
The lawsuit claims the user intentionally bypassed Grok's safeguards to create and distribute illegal content.
This incident highlights ongoing, critical challenges regarding AI safety, misuse, and content moderation.

stories.title: Third-party app stores coming to Google Play next week as Epic settlement withdrawn
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google Play will soon allow third-party app stores following the withdrawal of a settlement.
This change is a direct result of Google being bound by the court's full antitrust remedies.
The development signals a significant shift in the mobile app distribution ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes notable investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving a large developer base of 8.9 million.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed improvement based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents entirely on local, private hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for optimized performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
This represents a significant step toward faster, on-device AI inference for Apple users.

stories.title: Windows 0-day drops the same day Microsoft releases record number of patches
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical Windows 0-day vulnerability, named HiveLegacy, has been discovered.
The vulnerability is described as a 'powerful primitive' with potential for significant malicious use.
The discovery occurred concurrently with Microsoft releasing a large batch of security patches.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are advancing to the point of autonomously generating and submitting pull requests (PRs) to software projects.
The research shifts focus from individual PR outcomes to analyzing the adoption and management of these tools at the entire project level.
The study analyzes a large dataset of 25,264 agentic PRs across 2,361 popular GitHub repositories to investigate adoption patterns.

stories.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation
stories.author: Moslem Attar-Raouf
bullet_points: Traditional penetration testing is insufficient for AI-enabled systems.
Adversarial attacks in AI focus on altering system behavior rather than direct infrastructure compromise.
Attack vectors include manipulating prompts, sensor inputs, training data, and human-AI interaction loops.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are advancing to the point of autonomously generating and submitting pull requests (PRs) in software projects.
The research shifts focus from individual PR outcomes to the broader, project-level adoption and management of these AI tools.
The study analyzes a large dataset of over 25,000 agent-generated PRs across numerous popular GitHub repositories.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to expand model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance Claude Code's information retrieval abilities.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The key feature is running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: COMPUTER COPS: Inside the big business of selling AI to the police
stories.author: Webb Wright
bullet_points: The article examines the growing business of selling AI technology to law enforcement agencies.
It provides an insider look at a major industry event showcasing 'the future of policing in the digital age.'
The piece suggests a critical look at the implementation and implications of AI in police work.

stories.title: Move over, GPS: Navigation satellites in low-Earth orbit are making a comeback
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Xona is developing a new navigation system utilizing low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites.
The system is positioned as a potential alternative or complement to existing GPS technology.
The deployment plan involves launching 258 satellites into LEO.

stories.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
stories.author: Jie Li
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of current LLM interaction methods when Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning fails.
Proposes a new method, 'Deep Interaction,' to improve how humans interact with and correct large reasoning models.
Aims to move beyond simple re-generation or manual step-flagging to create more efficient error correction loops.

stories.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling
stories.author: Robert Ogburn
bullet_points: Addresses the critical industry need for rapid workforce reskilling, noting a significant increase in the time required to close skills gaps.
Proposes an end-to-end framework that integrates AI acceleration across five distinct stages of the learning lifecycle (knowledge acquisition to assessment).
Aims to overcome limitations of current frameworks by providing holistic, industry-validated solutions for professional upskilling.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components influence the preservation of 'rank' across network depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms to maintain gradient rank against rank-reducing operations.
The study demonstrates a trade-off where skip connections balance rank collapse against ensemble-like properties.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The research questions the common practice of reporting one-shot gains from agent-optimization methods.
It introduces the concept of continual learning, where optimization is applied recursively as new tasks and failures arise.
The core focus is determining if optimization-driven performance improvements compound over successive training iterations.

stories.title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
stories.author: Guillaume Lajoie
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of supervised learning in neural decoding, which requires paired behavioral labels.
The proposed method, MOJO, leverages unlabeled neural data to improve the generalizability of neural decoders.
Accurate neural decoding is crucial for advanced neurotechnologies like Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs).

stories.title: MetaPerch: Learning from metadata for bioacoustics foundation models
stories.author: Jenny Hamer
bullet_points: The research introduces 'MetaPerch' to enhance bioacoustic foundation models.
It focuses on leveraging readily available recording metadata (e.g., location, time) from citizen science platforms like Xeno-Canto.
The goal is to unlock untapped potential beyond relying solely on raw audio supervision for species detection.

stories.title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes
stories.author: Vanessa Smilansky
bullet_points: Researchers are investigating the utility of large genomic foundation models (like Evo 2) for biosecurity screening.
They tested the linear accessibility of biosecurity signals (specifically Antimicrobial Resistance - AMR) within frozen Evo 2 layer activations.
Minimal linear and attention probes demonstrated strong discriminatory power in detecting AMR using these pre-trained representations.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components influence the preservation of matrix rank across network depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms to maintain gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that expressive operations (matrix multiplications, non-linear activations) inherently reduce rank, and skip connections manage this trade-off.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether gains from agent-optimization methods compound over time.
Current reporting often treats optimization gains as one-shot improvements against a fixed benchmark.
The research addresses the practical need to evaluate agents where optimization is recursive as new tasks arise.

stories.title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
stories.author: Ben Zhou
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Hindcast' to evaluate LLM forecasters by backtesting against prediction markets.
It identifies two critical leakage channels in LLM forecasting evaluations: retrieval of post-event reports and training data contamination.
This work highlights methodological challenges in accurately assessing the predictive capabilities of large language models.

stories.title: Can an Old Dog Be Taught New Tricks? Taking LLMs Beyond Sentence Level Translation
stories.author: Alaina Brandt
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of current machine translation (MT) systems treating translation as a sentence-by-sentence task.
A new RAG-based system, PAT (Pragmatic Auto-Translator), is introduced to enable whole-document, corpus-informed translation.
PAT leverages context from comparable corpora (U.S. English and Latin American Spanish) and user specifications to improve translation quality.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether gains from agent-optimization methods are cumulative (compound) over time.
Current evaluations often treat optimization gains as one-shot, failing to simulate real-world, recursive deployment scenarios.
The research uses Terminal-Bench 2.0 to test the stability and compounding effect of iterative optimization on agents.

stories.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
stories.author: Frederic Bechet
bullet_points: Introduces DeepStress, a new framework designed to stress-test deep search agents.
Addresses the gap in research regarding the robustness of search agents when faced with poor-quality evidence.
Achieves controlled testing by replacing the retrieval module with a synthetic environment.

stories.title: SPyCE: Skill-Policy Co-evolution for Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Weijie Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces SPyCE, a novel approach for multimodal agents that iteratively manipulate visual evidence and use tools.
Addresses limitations in existing RL methods, which either force policies to relearn tool patterns or rely on static memory retrieval.
Proposes a co-evolution mechanism (Skill-Policy Co-evolution) to allow the policy to absorb reusable patterns from past experience.

stories.title: Post-Training Shifts Confidence: A Three-Stage Analysis of How SFT, RL, and OPD Shape Pre-, Intra-, and Post-CoT Calibration
stories.author: Xiaoyu Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how post-training methods (SFT, RL, OPD) affect the confidence calibration of Large Language Models (LLMs) during reasoning.
It moves beyond simple final-answer accuracy by introducing a three-stage calibration framework.
This framework analyzes confidence levels before, during, and after Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation, focusing on difficulty estimation and answer aggregation.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds, a key figure in Linux development, has commented on the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the kernel development process.
The discussion touches upon the integration and potential impact of generative AI tools in maintaining and evolving core operating system code.
This signals an emerging trend where cutting-edge AI technologies are being considered for highly critical, low-level software engineering tasks.
